h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר מ״ה Pesach — Maamar Mem Hei
And It Illuminated the Night: Faith Fixed in Israel's Heart at the Sea

p: וַיְהִי הֶעָנָן וְהַחֹשֶׁךְ וַיָּאֶר אֶת הַלָּיְלָה וְלֹא קָרַב זֶה אֶל זֶה כָּל הַלָּיְלָה
"And there was the cloud and the darkness, and it illuminated the night; and one did not come near the other all night long"
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, כ').
(Shemos 14:20).
אִיתָא בַּמְּכִילְתָּא
It is stated in the Mechilta
(עַיֵּין שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"ג, ז'):
(see Shemos Rabbah 23:7):
בִּיקְשׁוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לוֹמַר שִׁירָה, אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: יִשְׂרָאֵל נְתוּנִים בְּצָרָה וְאַתֶּם רוֹצִים לוֹמַר שִׁירָה?!
"The ministering angels sought to recite song [that night]; the Holy One, blessed is He, said to them: 'Israel are placed in distress, and you wish to recite song?!'"
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין מַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה צָרָה זוֹ מִשְּׁאָר הַצָּרוֹת שֶׁסָּבְלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא מָצִינוּ שֶׁנִּמְנְעוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לוֹמַר שִׁירָה?

Now one must understand: how did this distress differ from all the other troubles Israel endured, regarding which we do not find that the ministering angels were prevented from reciting their daily song?
וְגַם הֲלוֹא בַּמְּכִילְתָּא
And furthermore, surely in the Mechilta
(Beshalach 4)
אִיתָא עַל פָּסוּק "וַיָּאֶר אֶת הַלָּיְלָה" שֶׁהָיוּ הַמִּצְרִים רוֹאִים שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין וּשְׂמֵחִין!
it is stated on the verse "and it illuminated the night" that the Egyptians could see that Israel were eating, drinking, and rejoicing [all night]!
גַּם לְהָבִין מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר
Also, we must understand what is said [after the Splitting of the Sea]
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, ל"א):
(Shemos 14:31):
וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּה' וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ
"And they believed in Hashem and in Moshe His servant"
וַהֲלוֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר בְּמִצְרַיִם
surely it was already stated back in Egypt
וַיַּאֲמֵן הָעָם!
"And the people believed"!
וְגַם בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה הִבְטִיחַ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ לְמֹשֶׁה:
And later at the Giving of the Torah, Hashem, may He be blessed, promised Moshe:
וְגַם בְּךָ יַאֲמִינוּ לְעוֹלָם
"And also in you they will believe forever"
(שָׁם י"ט, ט')
אִם כֵּן נִרְאֶה שֶׁעַד עַתָּה עוֹד לֹא הָיָה הָאֱמוּנָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת!
which indicates that until then their faith was still not in full perfection!
גַּם לְהָבִין מַה שֶּׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה:
Also, we must understand what Moshe said [at the Burning Bush]:
וְהֵן לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ לִי וְגוֹמֵר
"And behold, they will not believe me, etc."
וְאָמְרוּ עַל זֶה
and concerning this they said
(Shabbos 97a)
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָמַר לְמֹשֶׁה: הֵם מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים, בְּנֵי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ
that the Holy One, blessed is He, said to Moshe, "They are believers, the children of believers—children of our father Avraham, peace be upon him, of whom it is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית ט"ו, ו'):
(Bereishis 15:6):
וְהֶאֱמִן בַּה'
'And he believed in Hashem'"
וְצָרִיךְ בֵּיאוּר: הָא כָּל טַעֲנַת מֹשֶׁה הָיָה שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ: לֹא נִרְאָה אֵלֶיךָ ה', וּמָה רְאָיָה מֵאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ שֶׁאֵלָיו נִרְאָה ה'?!
which requires explanation: Moshe's entire argument was that Israel would say "Hashem did not appear to you," so what proof is there from our father Avraham, to whom Hashem did appear?!
וְהִנֵּה הָרַמְבַּ"ן שָׁם דִּקְדֵּק עַל הַתַּרְגּוּם אוּנְקְלוֹס שֶׁתִּרְגֵּם עַל הַפָּסוּק "וְהֶאֱמִן בַּה' וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לּוֹ צְדָקָה":
Now the Ramban there pointed out regarding Targum Onkelos, who translated the verse "And he believed in Hashem, and He reckoned it to him as righteousness" as:
וְחַשְׁבַהּ לֵיהּ לִזְכוּ
"and He reckoned it to him as merit"
מַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה הָאֱמוּנָה הַזּוֹ מִשְּׁאָר הָאֱמוּנוֹת שֶׁהֶאֱמִין אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּכָל הַנִּסְיוֹנוֹת שֶׁנִּתְנַסָּה, וְלָמָּה חָשִׁיב דַּוְקָא זוֹ הָאֱמוּנָה לִזְכוּת?!
how did this act of faith differ from all the other acts of faith Avraham demonstrated throughout all his trials, and why was specifically this faith counted as merit?!
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן הוּא: דְּמַה שֶּׁהֶאֱמִין אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בַּה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּתֵּן לוֹ בֵּן, זֶה לֹא הָיָה נֶחְשָׁב לִזְכוּת;
However, the explanation is that the mere fact that our father Avraham, peace be upon him, believed Hashem, may He be blessed, would give him a son was not what was counted as merit;
רַק ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבְטִיחַ לוֹ וְאָמַר לוֹ: הַבֶּט הַשָּׁמַיִם וּסְפֹר אֶת הַכּוֹכָבִים וְגוֹמֵר כֹּה יִהְיֶה זַרְעֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר
rather, Hashem, may He be blessed, promised him and said, "Look at the heavens and count the stars, etc.—so shall your seed be, etc."
(ibid., v. 5)
וְיָדוּעַ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
and it is well known what they said in Midrash Rabbah
(בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה ב', י"ג):
(Bamidbar Rabbah 2:13):
נִמְשְׁלוּ לַכּוֹכָבִים וְנִמְשְׁלוּ לֶעָפָר: לַכּוֹכָבִים בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵם צַדִּיקִים
"[Israel] are compared to the stars and compared to the dust: to the stars when they are righteous"

וְזֶה הוּא נֶגֶד הַשֵּׂכֶל: כִּי תַּכְלִית בְּרִיאַת הָאָדָם הוּא לִהְיוֹת בַּעַל בְּחִירָה לִבְחוֹר בַּטּוֹב אוֹ בָּרָע, וְאִם בּוֹחֵר בַּטּוֹב מֵרְצוֹנוֹ זֹאת הוּא מַעֲלָתוֹ, וְאֵיךְ הִבְטִיחַ לוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כַּכּוֹכָבִים, דְּהַיְינוּ צַדִּיקִים?!

now this appears contrary to reason: since the entire purpose of man's creation is to possess free will to choose between good and evil, and his merit lies specifically in choosing good of his own volition, how could Hashem promise unconditionally that his descendants would be like the stars—meaning righteous?!
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הִיא: אַף שֶׁהָאָדָם הוּא בַּעַל בְּחִירָה, מִכָּל מָקוֹם אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ
Yet in truth, even though man has free will, nevertheless "were it not for the Holy One, blessed is He, helping him, he could not overcome [the evil inclination]"
(סוּכָּה נ"ב:),
(Sukkah 52b),

שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ אָדָם שֶׁמַּרְאֶה לִבְנוֹ אֵיזֶה חִידָה וּמַקְדִּים לוֹ כָּל הַקְדָּמוֹת עַד שֶׁכִּמְעַט אוֹמֵר לוֹ הַחִידָה, כְּדֵי שֶׁיָּבִין הַבֵּן וְיִהְיֶה נִקְרָא עַל שְׁמוֹ—כֵּן מִתְנַהֵג ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עִם הָאָדָם.

which is like a father who poses a riddle to his son and gives him every introductory clue until he practically tells him the answer, so that the son will grasp it and have the solution credited to his own name—so does Hashem, may He be blessed, conduct Himself with man.
וְזֶה הָיָה זְכוּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִין בַּה'

And this was the unique merit of our father Avraham, peace be upon him, that he believed in Hashem [that Hashem can grant spiritual illumination to make His children righteous even beyond their own merit]
[וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
[and so wrote the holy Zohar
וְהֶאֱמִן בַּה' — בְּהַהוּא דַּרְגָּא דְּאִתְיְיהִיב לֵיהּ, דְּמִתַּמָּן יֵיתֵי לֵיהּ זַרְעָא וְכוּלֵּי].
"'And he believed in Hashem'—in that supernal level granted to him from which offspring would come to him, etc."].
וְהִנֵּה כָּל הַשִּׁבְעָה יָמִים שֶׁפִּיתָּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה שֶׁיֵּלֵךְ בִּשְׁלִיחוּתוֹ, הָיָה טַעֲנָתוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה: בְּאֵיזוֹ זְכוּת אֶגְאָלֵם?
Now throughout all the seven days that the Holy One, blessed is He, persuaded Moshe to go on His mission, Moshe's argument was: "In what merit shall I redeem them?"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה שֶׁעֲבוּר זֶה לֹא יַאֲמִינוּ לִי, שֶׁהֵם מַרְגִּישִׁים בְּעַצְמָם שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם זְכוּת שֶׁיִּזְכּוּ בַּעֲבוּרוֹ לִגְאוּלָּה;

Meaning Moshe argued that for this very reason Israel would not believe him—because they felt within themselves that they possessed no merit whatsoever on account of which they could deserve redemption;

וְעַל זֶה הֵשִׁיב לוֹ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהֵם מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים, בְּנֵי אַבְרָהָם שֶׁהֶאֱמִין בִּי שֶׁאֲנִי יָכוֹל לִשְׁלוֹחַ הֶאָרָה בְּתוֹךְ לִבּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אַף שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מִצַּד עַצְמוֹ כְּלָל.

and to this Hashem, may He be blessed, answered him that they are believers, the children of believers—children of Avraham, who believed in Me that I am able to send an illumination into a person's heart even when he has nothing on his own side at all.
וְזֶה הָיָה אֱמוּנָתָם בְּמִצְרַיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיַּאֲמֵן הָעָם
And such was their faith in Egypt, as it is said, "And the people believed"
וְכֵן הָיָה, שֶׁשָּׁלַח לָהֶם ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הֶאָרָה וְאַהֲבָה יְתֵירָה וְהוֹצִיאָם מִשָּׁם.
and indeed so it happened, for Hashem, may He be blessed, sent them illumination and surpassing love and brought them out of there.
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם הִתְעוֹרְרוּת גַּם מִצַּד עַצְמָן, בְּלִי אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא
However, in truth, the will of Hashem, may He be blessed, was that they should also have an awakening from their own side, without an awakening from above
לָכֵן נִיטַּל מֵהֶם אוֹתָהּ הַהֶאָרָה שֶׁהָיָה לָהֶם בְּלֵיל רִאשׁוֹן דְּפֶסַח מִצַּד אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא, עַד יוֹם שִׁשִּׁי דְּפֶסַח בָּעֶרֶב, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ
therefore that illumination which they had received on the first night of Pesach from above was withdrawn from them until the evening of the sixth day of Pesach, of which it is said
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, י'):
(Shemos 14:10):
וּפַרְעֹה הִקְרִיב... וַיִּרְאוּ... כִּי צַר לָהֶם, וַיִּצְעֲקוּ אֶל ה'
"And Pharaoh drew near... and they saw... and they cried out to Hashem"
וְהִקְרִיב לִבָּם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לִתְשׁוּבָה
for he drew the hearts of Israel near to repentance
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ה'),
(Shemos Rabbah 21:5),
וְאוֹתָהּ הִתְעוֹרְרוּת הָיָה מִצַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּלִי אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא.
and that awakening came from Israel's own side without an awakening from above.
וּכְבָר דִּיבַּרְנוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ כַּמָּה מַדְרֵיגוֹת בֶּאֱמוּנָה, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
Now we have already discussed that there are many levels in faith, along the lines of what they said
(תָּמִיד כ"ח.):
(Tamid 28a):
יַחֲזִיק בֶּאֱמוּנָה יְתֵירָה
"He should hold fast to surpassing faith"
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ל"ז).
(as explained in Maamar 37).

וְהִנֵּה בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף שֶׁהִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לוֹמַר שִׁירָה מִתּוֹךְ מַעֲמַקֵּי לִבָּם, וְה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הִבִּיט בְּתוֹךְ לְבָבָם וְרָאָה שֶׁעֲדַיִין אֵינָם בְּגֶדֶר הָאֱמוּנָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, לָכֵן הוּצְרְכוּ לִתְשׁוּבָה שְׁלֵימָה, וּפַרְעֹה הִקְרִיב לִבָּם לִתְשׁוּבָה.

Now at the Splitting of the Sea, when Israel's time arrived to sing praise from the depths of their hearts, Hashem, may He be blessed, looked into their hearts and saw that they had not yet reached the level of complete faith; therefore they required complete repentance, and Pharaoh drew their hearts to repentance.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: וַיָּאֶר אֶת הַלָּיְלָה—וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהָיָה מֵאִיר וְהוֹלֵךְ אוֹר הָאֱמוּנָה בְּתוֹךְ לִבָּם בְּפוֹעַל עַד לִפְנוֹת בֹּקֶר, שֶׁנִּקְבַּע הָאֱמוּנָה בְּלִבָּם בֶּאֱמֶת.

And concerning this it is said, "And it illuminated the night"—meaning the light of faith progressively shone brighter within their hearts throughout the night until daybreak, when faith became truly and permanently fixed in their hearts.
וְלָזֶה הוּצְרַךְ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ לְנַהֵג בְּרוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה כָּל הַלָּיְלָה:
And for this reason Hashem, may He be blessed, had to drive the sea back with a strong east wind all night long:
הֲלוֹא אִם רָצָה כִּבְיָכוֹל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיִּבָּקְעוּ הַמַּיִם, כְּמוֹ רֶגַע הָפַךְ יָם לְיַבָּשָׁה!
for surely had Hashem, may He be blessed, so desired, in a single instant He could have turned the sea into dry land!
אַךְ הָיָה צָרִיךְ שֶׁיּוּקְבַּע הָאֱמוּנָה בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית תְּלוּיִם בְּמַאֲמָרוֹ וְאֵין שׁוּם טֶבַע בָּעוֹלָם זוּלַת הַנְהָגַת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ,

Yet it was necessary that faith be deeply ingrained in the heart of Israel that all of Creation depends solely upon His word and there is no independent "nature" in the world apart from the direct governance of Hashem, may He be blessed
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא
just as Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa said
(תַּעֲנִית כ"ה.):
(Taanis 25a):
מִי שֶׁאָמַר לַשֶּׁמֶן וְיִדְלוֹק יֹאמַר לַחֹמֶץ וְיִדְלוֹק
"He Who commanded oil to burn will command vinegar to burn"
שֶׁהָיָה בָּרוּר לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו שֶׁאֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר טֶבַע וְהֶרְגֵּל בָּעוֹלָם, רַק מַה שֶּׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מַשְׁפִּיעַ בָּזֶה כֹּחוֹ וְטִבְעוֹ בְּכָל עֵת וּזְמַן

for it was crystal clear before his eyes that nothing in the world operates by automatic nature or habit, only by Hashem, may He be blessed, continuously infusing His power and nature into it at every single moment
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ל"ב).
(as explained in Maamar 32).
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה נִקְבָּע בְּלִבָּם הָאֱמוּנָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, לֹא זָכוּ עוֹד לִקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף
And as long as faith was not yet completely fixed in their hearts, they had not yet merited the Splitting of the Sea
וְזֶהוּ: וַיְנַהֵג ה' רוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה כָּל הַלָּיְלָה,
and this is "And Hashem drove an east wind, strong, all the night,"
כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
along the lines of what is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית ב', ז'):
(Bereishis 2:7):
וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו נִשְׁמַת רוּחַ חַיִּים,
"And He breathed into his nostrils the soul of the breath (ruach) of life,"
וְתִרְגֵּם אוּנְקְלוֹס: לְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא,
which Onkelos translated "a speaking spirit (ruach memalela),"
וְהוּא נֶגֶד בְּחִינַת הָאַרְבַּע מַחֲנוֹת: אַחַר הָרוּחַ רַעַשׁ וְגוֹמֵר קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה וְגוֹמֵר
which corresponds to the four levels [in Eliyahu's vision]: "After the wind (ruach) an earthquake, etc., a still small voice, etc."
(מְלָכִים א' י"ט, י"ב)
(I Melachim 19:12)
וּבְחִינָה זוֹ הָיְתָה בְּעֵת הַשִּׁירָה, וּבַלַּיְלָה הָיָה בִּבְחִינַת "רוּחַ", וְזֶהוּ: וַיְנַהֵג ה' רוּחַ קָדִים עַזָּה וְגוֹמֵר.

for that highest level ["still small voice"] occurred at the time of the Song, whereas during the night they were still at the level of Ruach ("wind/spirit"), which is "And Hashem drove an east wind, strong, etc."
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹכְלִים וּשְׂמֵחִין, כִּי שִׂמְחָה הִיא שַׁיֶּכֶת לְמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חַיּוּת בְּתוֹךְ לְבָבוֹ,
And thus Israel were eating and rejoicing [that night], because joy belongs to one who has spiritual vitality within his heart,
אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הָיוּ נְתוּנִים עוֹד בְּצָרָה, כִּי לֹא הָיָה נִקְבָּע הָאֱמוּנָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת עַד לִפְנוֹת בֹּקֶר,
yet in truth they were still in a state of distress/constriction, because faith was not yet permanently fixed in perfection until daybreak,
וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
along the lines of what they said [regarding Yaakov]
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ע"ו, ב'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 76:2):
הַרְבֵּה קַטֵּיגוֹרִין יַעַמְדוּ מִכָּאן וְעַד גִּיחוֹן
"Many prosecutors will arise between here and Gichon"
אַף שֶׁכְּבָר הָיוּ מוּכָנִים לְמָשְׁכוֹ, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הָיָה יָרֵא שֶׁלֹּא יִגְרוֹם הַקִּטְרוּג.
for even though [Esav's men] were already prepared to draw him out of danger, Yaakov still feared lest heavenly prosecution take effect.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: בִּיקְשׁוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לוֹמַר שִׁירָה וְכוּלֵּי, עַל זֶה הֵשִׁיב לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: יִשְׂרָאֵל נְתוּנִים בְּצָרָה
And this is what they said: "The ministering angels sought to recite song, etc.," to which the Holy One, blessed is He, answered them, "Israel are placed in distress"
הַיְינוּ שֶׁעֲדַיִין לֹא נִקְבַּע בְּתוֹךְ לִבָּם הָאֱמוּנָה בִּשְׁלֵימוּת, וַהֲלוֹא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּם לוֹמַר שִׁירָה קוֹדֶם בַּתְּחִילָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
meaning that faith was not yet permanently fixed in their hearts, and surely Israel's time had come to recite song first before the angels, as it is said
(תְּהִלִּים ס"ח, כ"ו):
(Tehillim 68:26):
קִדְּמוּ שָׁרִים וְגוֹמֵר,
"The singers [Israel] went first, etc.,"
וְכָאָמוּר.
as stated.
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר: וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּה' וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ
And afterward [at daybreak] it says: "And they believed in Hashem and in Moshe His servant"
כִּי מֹשֶׁה הָיָה כְּלַל כָּל נִשְׁמַת שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וּכְדְאִיתָא בַּמְּכִילְתָּא
for Moshe was the root encompassing all six hundred thousand souls of Israel, as stated in the Mechilta
(בְּשַׁלַּח הַשִּׁירָה ט'):
(Beshalach, Shirah 9):
וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל פָּרוּ וַיִּשְׁרְצוּ — שֶׁנּוֹלַד שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא בְּכֶרֶס אֶחָד, וּמַנּוּ? מֹשֶׁה
"'And the Children of Israel were fruitful and swarmed'—teaching that six hundred thousand were born in a single womb, and who was that? Moshe"
כִּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה כְּלַל כָּל נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
for Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, was the collective root of all souls of Israel, and this is what they said in the Gemara
(בְּרָכוֹת ל"ג:):
(Berachos 33b):
וְכִי יִרְאָה מִילְּתָא זוּטַרְתָּא הִיא? אִין, לְגַבֵּי מֹשֶׁה מִילְּתָא זוּטַרְתָּא
"'Is fear of Heaven a small thing?' 'Yes, relative to Moshe it is a small thing'"
הַיְינוּ כִּי לְגַבֵּי מֹשֶׁה, דְּהוּא מְקוֹר נִשְׁמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל, הָיָה נוֹחַ לָהֶם לְהַגִּיעַ לִבְחִינַת יִרְאָה.
meaning that through attachment to Moshe, who is the source of Israel's souls, it became easy for them to reach the level of awe.

וְזֶהוּ: וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּה' וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ, הַיְינוּ שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁהֶאֱמִינוּ שֶׁמֹּשֶׁה עֶבֶד ה' וְהֵם עֲנָפִים מִמֶּנּוּ, עַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לֶאֱמוּנָה שְׁלֵימָה, וְלָזֶה זָכוּ בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף, וְכָאָמוּר.

And this is "And they believed in Hashem and in Moshe His servant": because they believed that Moshe is the servant of Hashem and that they are branches extending from him, through this they merited complete faith—and this they achieved at the Splitting of the Sea, as stated.

Rashi: "every day" — its evil increases daily.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chukas 6 — “The Ramban asked what merit there is for a prophet in believing the prophecy he heard from Hashem. We said that it refers to the promise ‘so shall your seed be,’ that they would be like the stars, meaning at a great level. This runs against the free choice given to man, so how could such a promise be? Nevertheless he believed, though it is above reason. And ‘He reckoned it to him’: to him precisely, according to his attribute, whose essence was effort from his own side and man acting by his own choice.” Connection: The same answer to the Ramban’s question; it adds that the faith counted as merit because it ran against Avraham’s own path of human effort and free choice.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Malbim, Bereishis 15:6 — “‘And he reckoned it to him as tzedakah’: when he examined and inquired by what merit Hashem would change the constellation for his sake, whether according to his deeds and merit or from kindness alone, it was too small in his eyes to think it came from his deeds by way of judgment; so he thought that Hashem did this for him out of the supernal tzedakah and the kindness of Hashem, not by merit. What Hashem does by way of judgment, according to merit, stops when people’s deeds turn bad; but what He does from the supernal tzedakah, without regard to deeds, never stops, since it does not depend on people’s merit and preparation.” Connection: Malbim also reads Avraham’s faith as trust in a kindness that does not depend on the recipient’s merit; he adds that such a gift cannot lapse, which explains why the promise held for his children.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Shevi'i shel Pesach 34 — “The whole praise Scripture gives in this miracle is for Israel’s faith: ‘And they believed in Hashem and in Moshe His servant.’ For one who truly believes that nature is in Hashem’s hand finds no wonder in a miracle, just as for Adam HaRishon there was no difference between the flowing of the sea and its splitting, since there was not yet any habit in the world. The main miracle of the Splitting of the Sea was that Hashem illuminated in Israel’s heart so great a faith that they believed the sea could split, and nature and habit caused them no astonishment.” Connection: Both read ‘vaya’aminu’ at the sea, with Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa’s oil and vinegar, as faith that there is no nature apart from Hashem; Sod Yesharim adds that nature is only habit and that this faith was itself the miracle.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 25a — R. Chanina ben Dosa's daughter had lit the Shabbos lamp from vinegar by mistake. "He said to her: My daughter, why should it trouble you? He Who told the oil to burn will tell the vinegar to burn. It was taught: it kept burning all day, until they took light from it for Havdalah." Rashi: they lit another lamp from it and put out the miracle lamp.

paragraphs.text: Bereishis Rabbah 76:2 — on Yaakov's fear despite God's promise: "Benayahu answered, 'Amen, so may Hashem say' — yet it had already been said, 'Behold, a son will be born to you…'! Rather, he said: Many accusers will arise between here and Gichon." So too a promise does not remove the fear of accusation.

paragraphs.text: Mechilta, Shirah 9 — "Rebbi once sat and expounded that a woman in Egypt bore six hundred thousand [in one birth]. A student asked: Who is greater, the world or a tzaddik?… When Yocheved bore Moshe, he was equal to the whole world… as it says, 'Then Moshe and the Children of Israel sang.'"

paragraphs.text: Berachos 33b — "Is fear of Heaven a small thing?… Yes; for Moshe it was a small thing. As R. Chanina said: A parable of a person asked for a large vessel: if he has it, it seems to him like a small vessel." Rashi (on "everything is in the hands of Heaven"): righteousness and wickedness alone are handed to man, who chooses fear of Heaven for himself.
